Ava —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We ran some numbers and want to explore a structure that keeps unit economics predictable as we ramp. Two asks from procurement: 1) a committed monthly corridor so our monthly per-token average can't spike > X if we hit the commit floor; 2) a true-up mechanism at quarter end so we don't over-credit if we under-utilize.

Conceptually we like a hybrid: marginal discounts for incremental volume above breakpoints (so we don’t overpay for early usage) but a blended floor guarantee if we miss commit by >10% — that would protect our finance team. Is that something Redwood would entertain?

I can share an example of our expected monthly distribution if that helps.

Emma

Emma —

Thanks — yes, we can do a hybrid corridor + true-up. High level proposal attached (pricing_model_v3.xlsx) and a short summary below:

- Commit: 25M tokens/month (12-month term)
- Breakpoints: 0-25M, 25M-100M, 100M+ tokens
- Marginal discounts apply at each breakpoint (you only get the lower unit price on the incremental tokens above each breakpoint)
- Corridor guarantee: if monthly usage < 90% of commit, we apply a blended floor rate for that month equal to an 80% floor of the expected blended rate across tiers (this protects HealthSync finance)
- Quarterly true-up: over/under usage reconciled at quarter end; credits applied to following invoice; clawbacks limited to 20% of a single quarter’s committed spend

Tradeoffs: corridor + blended floor increases revenue exposure on our side for under-utilization — we offset that with a slightly higher marginal price on top tiers and the clipped clawback. If you’d prefer a pure marginal-only model we can remove the corridor but that makes monthly finances more variable for you.

Next steps: please share your expected monthly distribution (or let us use the forecast you shared in the deck) and we’ll run a model. If this looks directionally right I’ll loop in Sergio to align on dedicated capacity guarantees and have legal redline the term sheet.

Attaching the spreadsheet and a draft term sheet.

Looping in a quick ops note: the marginal model is simpler to bill and audit in our system; corridor blended floors are doable but require a pre-defined lookback formula and a monthly usage signal. Two practical suggestions:

- Define the blended-floor calculation explicitly in the term sheet (we recommend: blended-floor-rate = max( floor_pct * average_effective_rate, minimum_unit_price ) ).
- Cap the monthly credit applied to invoices to avoid runaway refunds — we suggested 20% of the monthly invoice, with remaining credit applied over the next two invoices.

If HealthSync insists on a true blended guarantee with no cap, we’ll need an increased commit or a higher base price on the first breakpoint.

Ben
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference
